We present spatially resolved spectra in the J, H and 1.55–2.5 μm regions of Titan.

we have used the NIFS observations of Titan to determine the methane mixing ratio and the D / H ratio in the atmosphere of Titan.

the modeling of the near-IR spectra of Titan using a line-by-line radiative transfer code.
the development of a line list for methane in the near-in infrared that can be used for modeling Titan and other planetary spectra, and the application of the line list to the study of Titan.
the modeling of the near-infrared spectrum of Titan, and the use of that spectrum to determine the composition of Titan’s atmosphere.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Titan atmosphere has been accurately modeled in the near-instrument using a new line list, which can be used for future observations of Titan and other planetary atmospheres.
a combination of laboratory and observational data, and the latest line list for methane, can be used to model the near-infrared spectrum of Titan.

we have shown that it is possible to model the near-infrared spectrum of Titan using the latest laboratory data on methane, and that we have shown the need to use more sophisticated far-wing line shapes for modeling methane spectra.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the near-IR spectrum of a planet with a thick methane atmosphere, such as Titan, can be used as an important tool for determining the composition of the atmosphere.
the methane absorption coefficients in the 1–2 μm range are not well represented in current databases.
a high-quality line list of methane is required in order to accurately model spectra of Titan in these wavelength regions.
